stories.headline: Siliņa announces 'significant' windfall tax on fuel traders and price control measures
stories.summary: Prime Minister Evika Siliņa announced plans for a windfall tax on fuel traders and measures to reduce fuel prices, including excise tax cuts, in response to rising fuel costs from Middle East conflict. She described the tax as 'significant' but did not specify percentages.

stories.headline: Siliņa calls for EU to overcome Orbán's opposition to €90 billion Ukraine aid package
stories.summary: Prime Minister Siliņa urged the EU to overcome resistance from Hungary's Viktor Orbán and approve €90 billion in financial aid for Ukraine. At the European Council summit, Orbán blocked the loan package, leading to criticism from other EU leaders including Siliņa.

stories.headline: Siliņa presents annual government report to Parliament amid mixed reactions
stories.summary: Prime Minister Siliņa delivered her government's annual report to the Saeima, outlining achievements and plans. Opposition and coalition partners offered mixed reactions to the government's performance assessment, with some criticizing the lack of concrete solutions to ongoing problems.

stories.headline: Transport Minister Švinka survives no-confidence vote despite Rail Baltica criticism
stories.summary: Transport Minister Atis Švinka survived a no-confidence motion in Parliament by 50-48 votes. The opposition criticized his handling of Rail Baltica procurement issues, including a controversial tender where a cheaper bidder was excluded on technical grounds, prompting PM Siliņa to order an investigation.

stories.headline: Police arrest 21 people including officials in €1.5 million IT procurement fraud case
stories.summary: Police arrested 21 people, including state officials, in a criminal case involving suspected fraud in IT procurements worth €1.5 million. The European Public Prosecutor's Office initiated the case. Media reports suggest former Digital Development Agency director Jorens Liopa was among those detained.

stories.headline: President Rinkēvičs warns of no positive developments in Middle East conflict
stories.summary: President Edgars Rinkēvičs stated he expects nothing positive in the coming weeks regarding the Middle East war. He emphasized the interconnectedness of global conflicts and said Latvia has not received requests to participate in US-Israeli operations in the region.

stories.summary: Defense Minister Andris Sprūds met with German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius in Berlin to discuss regional security and defense cooperation. Sprūds also participated in signing cooperation agreements between companies from both countries and discussed drone testing plans for Latvia.

stories.headline: Latvian banking sector profits decline 33% to €379.6 million in 2025
stories.summary: Latvia's banking sector worked with profits of €379.6 million in 2025, down 33.3% from 2024. Bank deposits increased 8.1% to €27.6 billion, while the five largest banks maintained 87.16% market share in assets, according to Bank of Latvia data.

stories.headline: Government supports transferring supervision of non-bank lenders to Bank of Latvia
stories.summary: The government backed transferring oversight of non-bank credit institutions to the Bank of Latvia, consolidating supervision under one regulator instead of the current three institutions. The change is planned to take effect from January 2027.

stories.headline: Competition Council fines ss.lv €186,780 for abuse of dominant position
stories.summary: The Competition Council imposed a €186,780 fine on SIA 'SS', owner of online classified site ss.lv, for abuse of its dominant position in Latvia's online advertising market. The decision relates to anti-competitive practices in the classified advertising sector.
